[[File:Delong 2014.jpg|thumb|upright|Armin Delong in 2014]]
'''Armin Delong''' (29 January 1925 – 5 October 2017) was a Czech physicist and a pioneer of [[electron microscopy]] in Czechoslovakia.<ref name="VUT-obituary">{{cite web |date=7 October 2017 |title=Zemřel světově uznávaný fyzik Armin Delong |url=https://www.vut.cz/vut/aktuality-f19528/zemrel-svetove-uznavany-fyzik-armin-delong-d154630 |website=Brno University of Technology |language=cs}}</ref> Delong worked on electron microscopes that went into production at [[Tesla (Czechoslovak company)|Tesla Brno]]. The team's BS 242 tabletop microscope won a gold medal at [[Expo 58]] in Brussels. From 1961 to 1990, he was director of the Institute of Scientific Instruments of the [[Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="VUT-doctorate">{{cite web |title=Armin Delong |url=https://www.vut.cz/vyznamenani/doctor-honoris-causa-d328 |website=Brno University of Technology |language=cs}}</ref> His later work was focused on the development of compact [[Low-voltage electron microscope|low-voltage transmission electron microscopes]].<ref name="Technical-Museum">{{cite web |title=Slavnostní setkání při příležitosti 100. výročí narození prof. Armina Delonga |url=https://www.tmbrno.cz/media/tiskove-zpravy-2025/slavnostni-setkani-pri-prilezitosti-100-vyroci-narozeni-prof-armina-delonga-tz/ |website=Technical Museum in Brno |language=cs}}</ref>

Delong received the Czech government's Česká hlava award in 2005 and the [[Medal of Merit (Czech Republic)|Medal of Merit]] in 2015.<ref name="VUT-obituary" /> From April to June 1990, he served as Deputy Prime Minister of Czechoslovakia with responsibility for scientific and technological development.<ref name="VUT-doctorate" /><ref name="Government">{{cite web |date=25 September 2008 |title=Armin Delong |url=https://vlada.gov.cz/cz/clenove-vlady/historie-minulych-vlad/prehled-vlad-cr/1990-1992-csfr/marian-calfa-1/armin-delong-42099/ |website=Government of the Czech Republic |language=cs}}</ref>

== Scientific career ==
Delong studied electrical engineering in Brno, graduating in 1950.<ref>{{cite web |date=7 October 2017 |title=Zemřel český vědec Armin Delong, zakladatel elektronové mikroskopie |url=https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/clanek/domaci/zemrel-cesky-vedec-armin-delong-zakladatel-elektronove-mikroskopie-90882 |website=ČT24 |language=cs}}</ref> While still a student, he joined the research group of Aleš Bláha, who proposed that the group build an [[electron microscope]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Přikryl |first=Jan |date=16 January 2006 |title=Armin Delong: Člověk se musí zcela oddat věci |url=https://hn.cz/c1-17611930-armin-delong-clovek-se-musi-zcela-oddat-veci |work=Hospodářské noviny |language=cs}}</ref> Delong worked on the project with Vladimír Drahoš, Ladislav Zobač and other colleagues. The work led to the development of electron microscopes for manufacture by [[Tesla (Czechoslovak company)|Tesla Brno]]. Among them was the BS 242 tabletop microscope, which won a gold medal at the 1958 Brussels World's Fair.<ref>{{cite web |title=100 years since the birth of the father of Czechoslovak electron microscopy |url=https://www.vut.cz/en/but/news-f19528/100-years-since-the-birth-of-the-father-of-czechoslovak-electron-microscopy-d278383 |website=Brno University of Technology}}</ref>

From 1961 to 1990, Delong directed the Institute of Scientific Instruments of the [[Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences]] in Brno.<ref name="VUT-doctorate" /> The institute developed electron microscopes that were manufactured by [[Tesla (Czechoslovak company)|Tesla Brno]], with Vladimír Drahoš heading its electron optics department.<ref>{{cite web |title=Elektronová mikroskopie |url=https://isibrno.cz/cs/vyzkum/vyzkumna-oddeleni/elektronova-mikroskopie/zakladni-informace/ |website=Institute of Scientific Instruments of the Czech Academy of Sciences |language=cs}}</ref> Delong and Drahoš contributed to the development of the Tesla BS-540 [[transmission electron microscope]]. One of these instruments was installed at [[Brno University of Technology]] in 1974, where it was used for materials research and teaching.<ref>{{cite web |title=Historický mikroskop stále slouží ve výuce |url=https://www.fme.vutbr.cz/fakulta/zfsi/71964 |website=Brno University of Technology |language=cs}}</ref>

Delong continued his research at Delong Instruments, working with former students.<ref>{{cite news |last=Přikryl |first=Jan |date=16 January 2006 |title=Armin Delong: Člověk se musí zcela oddat věci |url=https://hn.cz/c1-17611930-armin-delong-clovek-se-musi-zcela-oddat-veci |work=Hospodářské noviny |language=cs}}</ref> His team developed the LVEM 5, a small [[transmission electron microscope]] that used an accelerating voltage of 5 kV.<ref name="Technical-Museum" /> Biological samples could be examined without heavy-metal staining because the microscope produced higher image contrast at low voltage.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bendayan |first1=Moise |last2=Londono |first2=Irene |last3=Paransky |first3=Eugene |year=2011 |title=Compartmentalization of Pancreatic Secretory Zymogen Granules as Revealed by Low-Voltage Transmission Electron Microscopy |journal=Journal of Histochemistry & Cytochemistry |volume=59 |issue=10 |pages=899–907 |doi=10.1369/0022155411418507 |pmc=3201130 |pmid=21832147}}</ref>
